title: Chemical change
competency: Describe chemical change and observe one in an experiment.

keywords.def: A change in chemical composition. New substances form.

en.text: A chemical change changes the chemical composition of a substance. New substances form. An iron nail going rusty, heating magnesium ribbon, a burning candle, photosynthesis and fermentation are chemical changes.

screens.title: The nail in water
screens.ask: A shiny iron nail is left in water for a few days. It turns reddish brown. Is it still just iron?
screens.after:
Rust is a new substance. It is reddish brown and flaky, not shiny and strong like iron.
Iron reacted with the air dissolved in the water.
A change that forms a new substance is a chemical change.

screens.title: 2.4.2 Chemical change
paras: A chemical change is a change in the chemical composition of a substance.
Examples: an iron nail going rusty, heating magnesium ribbon, a burning candle, photosynthesis, fermentation.

screens.title: Experiment 2.3: Rusting of iron
paras: Put a few clean, shiny iron nails in a test tube of fresh tap water.
Set the test tube in a rack. Observe after a few days.

screens.caption: An iron nail in water rusts after a few days.

screens.title: Chemical changes around us
screens.ask: Tap each one. What new substance forms?
items: Iron reacts with air and water. Reddish brown rust forms.
It burns with a bright white light. A white powder forms.
The wax burns. Carbon dioxide and water vapour form, with heat and light.
A plant uses sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make food (sugar) and oxygen.
Yeast changes sugar into alcohol and carbon dioxide, as in tella.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A change in chemical composition. New substances form.

screens.text: Experiment 2.3: what colour forms on the iron nail after a few days in water?
screens.why:
Tap water contains dissolved air.
Iron reacts with the oxygen in it.
The new substance, rust, is reddish brown.
This is the same colour as an old, rusty roof sheet.
screens.clue: Think of an old roof sheet.

screens.text: Experiment 2.3: is rusting a physical or a chemical change?
opts: Chemical: a new substance, rust, forms
screens.ans: Chemical: a new substance, rust, forms
screens.why:
Rust is a new substance with new properties.
It cannot easily be turned back into iron.
A change that forms a new substance is chemical.
It is not "only colour": the substance itself changed.

screens.text: Spot the chemical changes: tap every chemical change.
screens.why:
Ask: does something new form?
Fermentation of tella: sugar → alcohol and carbon dioxide. New.
Burning a candle: wax → carbon dioxide and water vapour. New.
Photosynthesis: water and carbon dioxide → food and oxygen. New.
Melting butter and tearing cloth form nothing new: physical.

screens.text: Two changes in one: a burning candle also melts. Which part is the chemical change?
opts: The wax burning to give carbon dioxide and water vapour
screens.ans: The wax burning to give carbon dioxide and water vapour
screens.why:
Melting wax: solid → liquid. Still wax, so physical.
Burning wax: wax reacts with oxygen in the air.
It forms carbon dioxide and water vapour, with heat and light: new substances.
So the burning is the chemical change.
screens.clue: Separate the melting from the burning.

test.text: Classify the change: rusting of iron is a …
test.why:
Iron reacts with air and water.
Rust is a new substance.
A new substance means a chemical change.

test.text: True or false? Fermentation is a chemical change.
test.why:
In fermentation, yeast changes sugar into alcohol and carbon dioxide.
These are new substances.
So fermentation is a chemical change. True.

test.text: Which of these is a chemical change?
opts: Heating magnesium ribbon until it burns
test.ans: Heating magnesium ribbon until it burns
test.why:
Boiling water, breaking glass and dissolving salt form nothing new: physical.
Burning magnesium ribbon gives a bright light and a white powder.
The powder is a new substance, so it is a chemical change.

test.ask: Complete the definition: a chemical change changes the chemical ___ of a substance.
test.why:
A chemical change makes new substances.
What the substance is made of changes.
That is its chemical composition.

test.text: Find the odd one out: which is NOT a physical change?
opts: Burning of wax in a candle
test.ans: Burning of wax in a candle
test.why:
Sublimation of iodine: solid → gas. Still iodine, so physical.
Tearing cloth and dissolving sugar in tea: physical too.
Burning wax forms carbon dioxide and water vapour: new substances.
So burning wax is a chemical change, not physical.

notes.text: Experiment 2.3: "lean shiny iron nails" is a misprint for "clean"; the materials list is cut off after "test" (test tube). Shown corrected.
